blocks.scene: CHAPTER 13: THE SANCTUARY OF FRESH INK
blocks.text: Outside the entrance to the secluded Appalachian retreat, Pierre lingered near the timber archway, peering cautiously through his round spectacles while Dravin and Eusacles stepped forward.

blocks.scene: CHAPTER 13: THE SANCTUARY OF FRESH INK
blocks.text: A middle-aged man in casual flannel waved with an easy, welcoming grin. "Don't be scared, bros," he called out warmly. "Don't be scared at all. We love fresh ink around here. We're happy to have you."

blocks.scene: CHAPTER 13: THE SANCTUARY OF FRESH INK
blocks.text: "Would we have remembered dying?" Dravin asked, adjusting his spectacles.

blocks.scene: CHAPTER 13: THE SANCTUARY OF FRESH INK
blocks.text: "You're not actually dead, but it depends on who you ask," the man chuckled, introducing himself as Mike. Hiding behind his leg was a shy young girl with solemn eyes. "I made it to the Margin around 2009. I was forty-two, and I've stayed forty-two. This is Lily—she's been eleven for a long time."

blocks.scene: CHAPTER 13: THE SANCTUARY OF FRESH INK
blocks.text: Eusacles closed his eyes, invoking his divine senses. A natural twenty flared in his blood, revealing the Margin not as a simple campground, but as a consecrated refuge shrouded by the mythological Mist, where residents carried faint, residual auras of both celestial and undead power.
Mike led the group past a row of rustic timber cabins, discussing the lodgings and community.

As they walked, Alfie suddenly tensed in Pierre's rucksack, his tiny wooden hands gripping the canvas rim. His painted eyes glazed over with haunting recollection: "I remember the dark... and the quiet... and lots of water, and many men screaming and shouting..."
Pierre gently rested a finger on Alfie's shoulder, murmuring softly: "Alfie... Alfie, it's okay. Bring it back."
"...and everyone going away under the water," Alfie finished quietly with a shudder.
"Bring it back, mate," Pierre whispered softly to Alfie. "You are not on the ship anymore."
Mike smiled with quiet compassion. "This is a fun doll," he observed, before turning his gaze toward Eusacles's wrist. "Who gave you that watch? I'm getting some sort of sense from it."
Eusacles glanced down at the heavy black timepiece. "As far as I know, it was a gift from my dad, given to me by my mother when I went off on my own. I never knew him."
"Fascinating," Mike nodded.
Settling into their guest cabin, the party prepared for sleep.

Suddenly, the wooden door swung open. A young woman with the side of her head shaved and eyes blazing with manic academic energy burst inside. "Sorry I'm late!" she announced breathlessly. "I heard there were new people! I am knee-deep in research and you all could really help out! Come on, I'll show you what I'm doing."

blocks.scene: CHAPTER 17: SATURDAY PANCAKES AND CONSPIRACY BOARDS
blocks.text: Pierre, already sitting in his nightwear with cucumber slices prepared for his face care routine, raised an eyebrow. "It can wait until the morning. I have already started my face care. I only have so many cucumbers."

blocks.scene: CHAPTER 17: SATURDAY PANCAKES AND CONSPIRACY BOARDS
blocks.text: Pierre gently closed the cabin door on the frantic researcher until the next day.

blocks.scene: CHAPTER 17: SATURDAY PANCAKES AND CONSPIRACY BOARDS
blocks.text: The next morning, a knock sounded at the door. Mike grinned from the porch. "Got some pancakes going—my thing on Saturdays! Naomi has been in my ear about getting you guys to check out what she's got going on."

blocks.scene: CHAPTER 17: SATURDAY PANCAKES AND CONSPIRACY BOARDS
blocks.text: At breakfast, Mike shared his personal theory: "I have a card from my daughter that says 'To Dad'. That's why I think I'm here. Something concrete was written down."

blocks.scene: CHAPTER 17: SATURDAY PANCAKES AND CONSPIRACY BOARDS
blocks.text: After breakfast, they entered Naomi's cabin. "Early on, Teddy was big into the fragments," she explained, leading them to her workspace. Her cot was neglected in favor of old CRT computer monitors streaming green code and a massive wall covered in pinned photos and red yarn connecting mythic events.

Inside the cabin, Naomi explained her algorithm for tracking temporal anomalies. "The fragments are leftovers from these crazy edits," she told them, gesturing to her notes. "Theodore told me they have some sort of energy attached to them—when he touched one, he experienced visions of different realities."

She pulled up an online academic thread showing a picture of the newly discovered Greek tablet on display in a museum. "There is a ton of discourse about what it translates to say," Naomi pointed out.
Dravin adjusted his wire-rimmed glasses in astonishment. "I actually wrote a paper on this tablet!"
Naomi scrolled down the screen, showing the fierce online debate and op-eds surrounding Dravin's research.

blocks.scene: CHAPTER 19: THE STOLEN TOMES & THE LOST ROADS
blocks.text: "Where is the closest fragment?" Dravin asked, studying the map pins.

blocks.scene: CHAPTER 19: THE STOLEN TOMES & THE LOST ROADS
blocks.text: Naomi pointed out three active leads: a mythic toy catapult in a UK pawn shop, a doctor giving a book tour, and the ancient Greek limestone tablet at the state museum in North Carolina.

blocks.scene: CHAPTER 19: THE STOLEN TOMES & THE LOST ROADS
blocks.text: Pierre pulled out the ancient books he had taken from the Library of the Fates.

blocks.scene: CHAPTER 19: THE STOLEN TOMES & THE LOST ROADS
blocks.text: "Books are for the public to read," Pierre insisted innocently with a Gallic shrug.

blocks.scene: CHAPTER 19: THE STOLEN TOMES & THE LOST ROADS
blocks.text: Examining an ancient Greek passage in the volume, Naomi and Dravin translated a reference to the **Lost Roads**—ancient shifting planar pathways tied to mythic origins. "This book mentions the Lost Roads... and in a way, we are on a lost road now," Pierre noted thoughtfully.
Pierre examined the photos of the limestone artifact. "This tablet is something I can see as a reason I am here."
"Let's start with the Greek tablet," Eusacles agreed. "At least we have the potential of the good old doctor translating it."
"This tablet," Dravin nodded eagerly, his academic curiosity fully ignited.

Before embarking on their mission, the group tested their coordination during a brief supply run. Alfie drew his needle rapier, indignantly protesting anytime anyone referred to him as a doll: "Quit calling me a doll!"

Another truck pulled up carrying Mike, Teddy, Rosa, and Anna, all laughing heartily at the spirited exchange. Returning to the Margin's porch, Naomi was there to welcome them back, confirming everyone was ready.

blocks.scene: CHAPTER 22: AT THE THRESHOLD OF THE LOST ROADS
blocks.text: The party gathered at the edge of the Margin near the maintenance shed, standing on the edge of the threshold to begin their journey through the Lost Roads toward North Carolina.

blocks.scene: CHAPTER 22: AT THE THRESHOLD OF THE LOST ROADS
blocks.text: Pierre walked over to Dravin and Eusacles, adjusting his rucksack as they prepared to step into the shifting dimensional mist.
